provenance.current_linkage_note: One live official page was verified for this topic on 2026-09-02. The National Commission for Backward Classes About Us page on the commission's own website, read on that date, records that the commission was initially constituted by the central government under the National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993 dated 2 April 1993 and had so far been reconstituted seven times up to 2016; that the Act of 1993 has been repealed through the National Commission for Backward Classes (Repeal) Act, 2018 dated 14 August 2018; that the present eighth commission has been accorded constitutional status and was constituted through the Constitution (One Hundred and Second Amendment) Act, 2018 dated 11 August 2018, whereby Article 338B was inserted, forming a commission for the socially and educationally backward classes to be known as the National Commission for Backward Classes; and that the commission consists of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three other Members in the rank and pay of Secretary to the Government of India, whose conditions of service and tenure of office were notified by a Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment notification dated 23 August 2018. Those statements are used only for what they say, and no case, complaint, recommendation, sitting or list-revision figure is inferred from them. Four further official checks were attempted on the same date, namely a departmental scheme identifier that returned a not-found page, a second departmental scheme identifier that returned the same not-found page, a departmental scheme listing page that returned navigational content only and a departmental sector-information page that returned navigational content only, so nothing was read or used from them and no secondary summary, coaching site or news report has been treated as an official source. The package therefore relies on that verified page together with the dated official anchors already carried by the repository owners, each cited with its issuing instrument or decision date: Article 15(4) and Article 16(4) for special provision and reservation; Article 342A for the Central List, with the President specifying and Parliament alone varying it; Article 338B for the national commission; the Constitution (One Hundred and Second Amendment) Act, 2018 and the Constitution (One Hundred and Fifth Amendment) Act, 2021, the second of which restored the power of States to prepare their own lists for State purposes after the 2021 Maratha reservation reading; the Constitution (One Hundred and Third Amendment) Act, 2019 inserting Article 15(6) and Article 16(6) for reservation of up to ten per cent for economically weaker sections outside the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes and the other backward classes; the decision in Indra Sawhney against Union of India of 1992 upholding twenty-seven per cent reservation, mandating the creamy-layer exclusion for the other backward classes only and stating the ordinary fifty per cent ceiling; the creamy-layer income and wealth ceiling of eight lakh rupees notified in September 2017, applied over three consecutive years on top of notified parental service and status categories and with salary and agricultural-land income excluded from simple clubbing; the Department of Personnel and Training notification dated 31 January 2019 setting a gross annual family income below eight lakh rupees together with the asset limits of five acres of agricultural land, a residential flat of 1,000 sq ft, a residential plot of 100 sq yards in a notified municipality and 200 sq yards elsewhere; the decision in Janhit Abhiyan against Union of India of November 2022 upholding that reservation by a majority of three to two, with the recorded majority reasoning and the recorded dissent; the umbrella education-support framework PM-YASASVI of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment for students of the other backward classes, the economically backward classes and the denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic tribes; the Rohini Commission of 2017 examining sub-categorisation, with implementation recorded as pending as of mid-2026; the last published all-caste census tables of 1931 and the unreleased and unvalidated caste data of the Socio Economic and Caste Census of 2011; and the recorded status as at 21 July 2026 that the Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs decided on 30 April 2025 to include caste enumeration, that the 2027 Census is planned as an all-digital exercise and that the first-phase houselisting window was notified for 1 April to 30 September 2026. No population share, beneficiary count, certificate count, seat-fill rate, scholarship disbursement, budget or expenditure figure is asserted, no National Family Health Survey, Periodic Labour Force Survey, National Sample Survey, NITI Aayog or Sustainable Development Goal value is asserted, no legal or constitutional provision is invented or upgraded in status, no judicial observation is converted into a binding holding or a legislated rule, no pending report or bill is described as enacted or implemented, and no previous-year question, official answer key or option is asserted or inferred.
provenance.pyq_status_note: The audited routing ledgers route no General Studies Mains demand and no objective demand to this owner for the covered years, and that zero is reported openly rather than concealed or filled with a manufactured demand card. The four audited ledgers consulted are the Mains routing ledgers for 2018 to 2023 and for 2024 to 2025 and the Prelims routing ledgers for 2018 to 2023 and for 2024 to 2025, and neither the Basic owner nor the Advanced owner for this topic carries a generated previous-year integration block, which is itself consistent with that zero. Both owners state independently that there is no confirmed direct 2024 or 2025 General Studies Paper II Mains question specifically on the other backward classes or the economically weaker sections in the audited local previous-year texts, and this package adopts exactly that position. The two nearest neighbouring demands are the 2018 General Studies Paper II question on the Scheduled Caste commission and reservation in minority institutions and the 2022 General Studies Paper II question on the backward-class commission moving from a statutory to a constitutional body, and the audited 2018-2023 Mains routing ledger routes both to the Polity commissions owner together with the consolidated body-design owner, so no ownership is claimed over either here; reservation doctrine such as the ordinary fifty per cent ceiling and the constitutional validity reasoning for the economic criterion is likewise routed to the Polity special-provisions owner and is cross-linked rather than duplicated. The practice in this package therefore consists of six original Mains questions with model solutions, each written to the repository's examiner-grade standard using the claim, named evidence, analysis and qualification pattern, together with eighty original objective questions on a strict A-B-C-D rotation. Each model solution opens with its analytical claim so that the evidence which follows does argumentative rather than decorative work. The locally held OCR-searchable official General Studies papers were read only to confirm that no question on this owner's subject matter is routed here; no question was invented from them, no marking scheme or page precision was imported and no official answer key is claimed for any question anywhere in this package.
